title: nuc-seq / SNES
reason: scope:SNES: The poster explicitly groups SNES as a target. SNES primary full text supports the depicted G2/M selection/nuclear-lysis/Phi29-MDA preparation, and the Synthesis intermediate is retained at this common amplification-depiction level. SNES also supports G1/0 nuclei, which are not a drawn alternative here. This operation instance uses G2/M-derived material and is assigned only to the supported G2/M SNES implementation. SNES is an exome-sequencing method because of downstream library construction and exome capture; the row itself ends before those interfaces. Applicability of the separately drawn S1-nuclease operation to SNES is unestablished: the secondary drawing is specifically captioned nuc-seq, and the inspected SNES primary text describes MDA and subsequent library construction without identifying S1 treatment. Omitting op_s1 from this method assignment records that gap, not evidence that SNES never uses it.

candidate.title: nuc-seq / SNES
candidate.scope: The central poster row labeled nuc-seq / SNES is the extraction unit. Its connected route is Cell sorting from G2/M distribution (Cell 1–3 with only the middle candidate retained), Lyse cell, Nucleus, Phi 29, Limited amplification, Synthesis, S1 nuclease, DNA. The three cell-to-genome icon arrows under Single cell genome describe separate single-cell genomic targets without a named preparation transformation; no transfer arrow connects that motif to the main route. The adjacent MIDAS, MALBAC, OS-Seq and right-margin chemistry are outside this unit. The graph describes a single-nucleus genomic DNA amplification component ending at amplified DNA, rather than a finished adapter-bearing library. Primary-supported interpretation resolves the G2/M-versus-S-phase wording and nuclear lysis interface, while preserving the drawn observations in corrections. nuc-seq and SNES remain distinct named targets. The drawn G2/M preparation is supported within both methods, but is not the full applicability of SNES, which also accepts G1/0 nuclei. The independently captioned nuc-seq drawing supports the complete poster route at schematic level; SNES applicability of the separately drawn S1 treatment remains unestablished. Downstream library construction and exome capture clarify target representation but are not added as unshown operations.

research_questions.question: The poster explicitly groups SNES as a target. SNES primary full text supports the depicted G2/M selection/nuclear-lysis/Phi29-MDA preparation, and the Synthesis intermediate is retained at this common amplification-depiction level. SNES also supports G1/0 nuclei, which are not a drawn alternative here. This operation instance uses G2/M-derived material and is assigned only to the supported G2/M SNES implementation. SNES is an exome-sequencing method because of downstream library construction and exome capture; the row itself ends before those interfaces. Applicability of the separately drawn S1-nuclease operation to SNES is unestablished: the secondary drawing is specifically captioned nuc-seq, and the inspected SNES primary text describes MDA and subsequent library construction without identifying S1 treatment. Omitting op_s1 from this method assignment records that gap, not evidence that SNES never uses it.
